title: Rambo: master arrangement and source programs

coverage.description: Two adjacent 128-call source units only. All note rows intersecting each unit are included, with program state at entry. Event ends are the next executed score transitions, not audible-tail boundaries. Role labels are editorial descriptions of source allocation. This is not whole-song form, a complete audible-state reconstruction, or composer-intent evidence.

parts.title: Lead
parts.role: Foreground pulse line on source physical voice 1

parts.title: Bass
parts.role: Lower pulse accompaniment on source physical voice 2

parts.title: Arpeggio / modulator
parts.role: Computed chord program on source physical voice 3; also the lead's oscillator modulator during coupled source gestures

instruments.title: Short pulse lead
instruments.description: A short gate countdown articulates the repeating pulse lead; the entry selects no new PWM or pitch program. This label describes the observed program state, not a recovered instrument name.
behavior: Pulse control $41; attack/decay $01, sustain/release $E7.
No newly selected PWM program; the event retains its exact entering sound state.
No newly selected frequency program; this does not erase a retained entering program state.
Gate countdown 4 calls and sound lifetime 12 calls are separate; next-row boundaries do not measure the audible release.

instruments.title: Moving pulse bass
instruments.description: The bass pulse width advances through two additive phases while the score supplies its low-note rhythm. This label describes the observed program state, not a recovered instrument name.
behavior: Pulse control $41; attack/decay $00, sustain/release $C9.
PWM program flags $05, delay 0 calls, phase lengths 10/255 calls; additive steps are retained in the program data.
No newly selected frequency program; this does not erase a retained entering program state.
Gate countdown 5 calls and sound lifetime 50 calls are separate; next-row boundaries do not measure the audible release.

instruments.title: Descending saw chord: 0, 3, 8, 12
instruments.description: A sawtooth voice cycles source pitch offsets 0, 3, 8, 12 semitones from its base note, one tone at a time. This label describes the observed program state, not a recovered instrument name.
behavior: Sawtooth control $21; attack/decay $00, sustain/release $99.
No newly selected PWM program; the event retains its exact entering sound state.
Descending source chord-byte pitch program; its pitch sequence is computed after the base-note entry, not simultaneous independent notes.
Gate countdown 5 calls and sound lifetime 40 calls are separate; next-row boundaries do not measure the audible release.

passages.title: Short pulse phrase over bass and arpeggio
passages.description: Follow the short pulse lead against the moving pulse bass and the descending saw chord figures. The carried-in sync pulse hands over to the short-note lead at the next source call.

dependencies.description: These three physical voices share one chip's filter, master volume and mono output. The source uses no per-voice pan.
The carried-in lead has control $43; its sync dependency on arpeggio persists through source call 5426, before the next row replaces it.

passages.title: The lead phrase repeats over a shifted bass

recurrence.description: The lead reuses the same graph nodes, relative entry times and base pitches. The bass reuses its rhythm and graph nodes eight semitones higher; this is not an identical whole-mix repeat.

passages.description: Follow the same short pulse lead as the bass repeats its rhythm eight semitones higher; the chord-program state changes with the accompaniment. These are observed source relationships, without a claim about Galway's intention.
